items.title: Trump says US 'low-keying it' with Iran
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump signaled Sunday he is prepared to let economic pressure mount against Iran, apparently backing away from ordering more military strikes even as Teheran issues tough demands. Axios said Trump did not express any frustration Sunday with Iran's delaying an agreement to open up the Strait of Hormuz. It's like a chess game," Trump said of US dealings with Iran.

items.title: Airbus sees supply chain recovery as it targets 870 deliveries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Airbus is confident that its supply chain is showing signs of recovery as the aircraft manufacturer works towards its target of delivering around 870 commercial aircraft this year. The deliveries comprised 44 A220s, 271 A320 Family aircraft, 10 A330s and 26 A350s. Stanley said Airbus delivered 81 aircraft to 45 customers in May 2026.

items.title: Over 200 firefighters battle blaze in southern France
items.summary: The fire broke out around 12.45pm (1045 GMT) in the Lozere region, about 140 kilometres (85 miles) northwest of Montpellier. Officials said it might have been sparked by a vehicle catching fire on a local road. A Lozere fire service spokesman said their combined efforts had helped "contain the blaze and save two homes" that were directly threatened.

items.title: Medan Selera 223 traders pin hopes on RM40.5m flood plan [WATCH]
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Traders at Medan Selera 223 are hoping that a RM40.5 million flood mitigation plan will end costly flash floods. "I am satisfied with what MBPJ presented because the plan was clear," said Medan Selera PJ Lestari Traders Association chairman Farahanim Ahmad, 43. The Petaling Jaya City Council's (MBPJ) plan will, among others, involve high-capacity drainage upgrades, automated flood gates, runoff pumping stations and an underground water detention pond to absorb downpours.

items.title: Gaza plan rejected by Netanyahu 'only way forward': Trump board head
items.summary: Netanyahu earlier told his cabinet that he rejected the plan, under which Hamas would hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing body and Israel would start a withdrawal from the war-ravaged territory. But Mladenov maintained that Israel would eventually pull out if there were verified disarmament. He said the disarmament would involve all Hamas weapons, down to Kalashnikov rifles.

items.title: If police stop you in Malaysia, here's what you should know
items.summary: What if they ask you to follow them to the police station? Can police check your phone? A police officer stops you.

items.title: Pulau Tuba’s authentic village life pitched as Langkawi’s next big tourism secret
items.summary: LANGKAWI, Aug 10 — Pulau Tuba has the potential to attract more domestic and international tourists with its authentic traditional village atmosphere and unique cultural experiences, said Kedah Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin. He said despite Langkawi recording more than three million tourist arrivals, visitor numbers to Pulau Tuba remained relatively low, highlighting the island’s untapped potential as a “hidden gem”. “Tourist arrivals in Langkawi reach the millions, yet only a small number visit Pulau Tuba.

items.title: 'Fewer South Koreans are eating kimchi'
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korean adults are eating less kimchi despite the growing global popularity of the country's signature side dish, Yonhap News Agency reported yesterday. According to a joint study by researchers from Chung-Ang University, Jeju National University and the World Institute of Kimchi, the proportion of Korean adults who reported eating no kimchi within the past 24 hours rose from 11.7 per cent in 2010 to 22.7 per cent in 2024. Non-consumption rates among men doubled from 10.2 per cent to 20.6 per cent, while rates for women climbed from 13.1 per cent to 24.8 per cent.

items.title: Demand for Japanese cuisine lifts exports to Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The warm reception to Japan's cuisine will boost its agricultural and seafood exports to Malaysia, said Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) Kuala Lumpur managing director Koichi Takano. "Malaysia now ranks 10th among all export destinations for Japanese agricultural, forestry, fishery and food products, up from 13th place previously. "The increase in Japanese restaurants globally demonstrates that Japanese cuisine has become well established internationally."

items.title: Round-the-clock Prasarana services for National Day
items.summary: Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the company was committed to supporting this year's celebrations in Putrajaya. Fahmi also confirmed that Malaysia Day celebrations would be held at the Borneo Cultural Centre in Kuching, Sarawak, describing its scale as comparable to Penang's PICCA Convention Centre, which hosted last year's event. Meanwhile, Fahmi said this year's Jalur Gemilang distribution features magnetic flags for vehicles.

items.title: 1,524 wild animal attacks since 2020, says Perhilitan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Wildlife and National Parks Department recorded 1,524 cases of human-wildlife conflict between 2020 and July this year. Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the incidents resulted in 1,470 injuries and 54 deaths. "These conditions force wildlife to seek new roaming areas near forests, plantations and neighbouring villages.

items.title: Moderate earthquake hits southern Sumatra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.3 on the Richter scale struck southern Sumatra, Indonesia at 11.15pm last night. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in a statement said the earthquake was centred at coordinates six degrees South and 102.4 degrees East with a depth of 78km. It is located 239km southwest of Pagar Alam, Indonesia, according to the statement.

items.title: Pas ready to explain PN crisis complaint to RoS, says Takiyuddin
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas is ready to provide an explanation to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) if the regulator seeks clarification over a complaint concerning the crisis within Perikatan Nasional (PN), said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan. Takiyuddin, who is also PN secretary-general, said Pas was currently unaware of the nature of the complaint referred to by Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz. On cooperation within PN, Takiyuddin said component parties should use the coalition for the benefit of all its members.

items.title: Pas to invite Umno leaders to annual muktamar
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas will invite Umno leaders to attend its 72nd muktamar in Kelantan next month. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the invitation letter would be sent soon. He added that next month's muktamar would also mark Pas' 75th anniversary.

items.title: Tibetan activist's final act puts forgotten struggle in spotlight
items.summary: Rangzen, a longtime Tibetan activist aged 52, had set himself ablaze, and died. But Rangzen's fellow exiled Tibetans, who have struggled to win international attention for their opposition to Chinese communist rule, greeted his passing with anguish and respect. "His passing has left many of us Tibetans with the fervour to act," said Jampa Choedup, a monk who had known Rangzen since 1997 and saw him the day before his death.

items.title: Five bodies hanging from bridge revive Mexico town's drug war fears
items.summary: POZOS DE GAMBOA, Mexico: Horrific drug violence plagued the Mexican state of Zacatecas for years, until relative calm set in. Then one morning in July this small town woke up to find five bodies dangling from a bridge – a grim calling card that showed the bloodshed never really left. These days in Pozos de Gamboa, a Zacatecas town of 5,000 that is known for growing beans, people are terrified.

items.title: The Iran war has exposed the world's energy vulnerability
items.summary: Progressives typically say the conflict underscores the need to accelerate the transition to renewables and electric vehicles (EVs), while conservatives argue it shows the need to develop more fossil fuel production outside the Middle East. Australia, the world's leading diesel importer, offers a prime example of the dilemma facing fuel importers. Australia relies on imports for about 80 per cent of its liquid fuel needs.

items.title: NST Leader: Malaysia must first answer how many migrant workers it needs
items.summary: Tenaganita, a labour rights organisation, suggests that regularising existing migrant workers might be the solution rather than importing more from overseas. But first, how many migrant workers are there in the country? There aren't reliable figures available, especially for undocumented workers.

items.title: Aruz, Ferrari drivers call truce, but police probe rolls on
items.summary: Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said, however, that police would continue investigating the incident, which occurred around 11am yesterday . "Both parties met and held private discussions at their own request, without the involvement or intervention of police," he said in a statement today. Johari said despite the amicable settlement, it would not affect the police investigation.

items.title: 'Duit kutu': RM1.7mil losses, 35 reports lodged
items.summary: JITRA: Police have received 35 reports involving a woman linked to duit kutu (informal money pool), with total losses amounting to RM1.7 million. Kubang Pasu district police chief superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the reports were lodged by victims aged between 23 and 53. Following this, the woman's 62-year-old father lodged a police report at the Bukit Kayu Hitam police station last Monday after failing to trace his daughter, son-in-law and grandchild.

items.title: 60,000 illicit cigarettes seized in Kota Baru, Vellfire driver arrested
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 60,000 cigarettes suspected to be duty-unpaid, valued at RM112,200, and arrested a 37-year-old driver after intercepting a Toyota Vellfire at the shoulder of the Pasir Tumboh Bridge early this morning. Southeast Brigade GOF Commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the suspect was stopped during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan at about 1.30am after he failed to produce relevant documentation for the goods and tested positive for drugs. Radzi said the suspect and all seized items were handed over to the Criminal zInvestigation Department and Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department of the Kota Baru district police Headquarters.

items.title: Sabah to acquire 30pct stake in 2 new oil and gas fields, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will acquire a 30 per cent stake in two new oil and gas fields off the state's east coast, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the state government was also finalising the acquisition of a 40 per cent equity stake in a floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) facility project in Sabah. Hajiji said the state government continued to focus on strengthening its financial performance and increasing revenue collection as an important foundation for Sabah's development.

items.title: MOH adds boat services to improve healthcare access for Orang Asli in Hulu Perak
items.summary: IPOH: The Health Ministry (MOH) has introduced additional boat services to strengthen healthcare access in Hulu Perak, reducing emergency response times for Orang Asli residents in the Kemar Resettlement Scheme (RPS) in Gerik. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the RM350,000 Medic Boat 8 was vital for more than 4,500 Orang Asli residents in the area, who depend entirely on waterways as their main means of access and transport. "The 12-passenger multipurpose boat will add to the MOH's existing fleet of six boats.

items.title: Sabah to channel RM1.5bil interim payment into infrastructure, welfare
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will use the increased interim payment from Putrajaya to improve infrastructure and strengthen welfare initiatives for the people, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the Sabah government had accepted an interim arrangement under which the payment, previously set at RM26 million, had been increased to RM1.5 billion from this year. On Sabah's 40 per cent entitlement to federal revenue derived from the state, Hajiji said the government would continue to pursue its right, as enshrined in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), through government-to-government negotiations with the Federal Government.

items.title: Strong winds fuel Bromo wildfire, blaze spreads to 520ha
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Mount Bromo wildfire has surged out of control, spreading across 520 hectares as strong winds fanned flames from the slopes into the savanna of East Java, authorities confirmed Sunday. Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park (TNBTS) Authority head Rudijanta Tjahja Nugraha said the blaze flared up again on Saturday night, burning not only the slopes but also the savanna. "The fire grew larger due to fairly strong winds since yesterday afternoon, allowing it to spread rapidly from the upper slopes towards the lower areas," he said, according to Antara News Agency.

items.title: Thai school shooting: Students, teachers mourn 12-year-old victim
items.summary: Investigators are still seeking a motive, but police said on Sunday the boy had watched violent videos online and once brought a BB gun to school. Officials said earlier he faced academic-related stress and a classmate said he was bullied. She died in hospital on Saturday after suffering gunshot wounds at the school, police said.

items.title: Alleged cartel boss Kinahan extradited from UAE to Ireland
items.summary: DUBAI: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates handed over alleged transnational cartel boss Daniel Kinahan to face trial in Ireland, the Gulf country's official media reported on Sunday. Kinahan "was extradited by the UAE to the Irish authorities at their formal request to face prosecution for offences related to transnational organised crime, including allegations of leading a criminal organisation, murder and illicit drug trafficking," said the report. Kinahan was arrested in Dubai in April after a warrant was issued in Ireland for "alleged serious organised crime offences" and lost appeals against extradition.

items.title: Air India pilot flagged for confirmatory drug test after 300ft plunge
items.summary: MUMBAI: India's aviation ministry said Sunday that an Air India pilot whose flight plunged dramatically in turbulence injuring 17 passengers and crew is undergoing a "confirmatory" psychoactive drug test. "The screening test in respect of the Pilot-in-Command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing," it said. The ministry said the flight has been classified as a "Serious Incident", and that India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has launched an investigation.

items.title: Upko's entry strengthens Sabah political stability, says Hajiji
items.summary: PENAMPANG: Upko's entry into Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) will further strengthen political stability in Sabah, said GRS chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said the party, led by its president Datuk Ewon Benedick, would also enhance cooperation among local parties in efforts to develop Sabah. GRS comprises Parti Gagasan Rakyat, Parti Cinta Sabah, LDP, PBS, Harapan and Upko.

items.title: Syria, Russia reach deal to turn military bases into training centres
items.summary: DAMASCUS: Syria said on Sunday that it reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war. Syria's official SANA news agency quoted the foreign ministry as saying that Hmeimim airbase and Tartus naval base, Russia's only two official military bases outside the former Soviet Union, would be turned into "joint training and capacity-building centres, within new arrangements that preserve mutual interests." Russia was a key Assad ally during Syria's 13-year conflict, and provided vital military support that kept the former leader's forces in power.

items.title: Final LMSB2 vessel Tunku Osman Jewa launched in Turkiye
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The navy's third Littoral Mission Ship Batch 2 (LMSB2) vessel has been named Tunku Osman Jewa and launched at Istanbul Shipyard, Turkiye, today. The vessel was named in honour of the late General Tan Sri Tunku Osman Tunku Mohammad Jewa, a Kedah royal family member who was the first armed forces chief appointed from among Malaysians. The Defence Ministry delegation was led by armed forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

items.title: Gaza death toll rises to 73,386 amid ongoing Israeli aggression
items.summary: GAZA: Health authorities reported on Sunday that the death toll from Israel's ongoing aggression on the Gaza Strip has risen to 73,386, with 174,250 others injured, since Oct 7, 2023, the Palestine News and Info Agency (WAFA) reported. They said the death toll since the ceasefire took effect on Oct 11, 2025, has reached 1,258, while the number of injuries has risen to 4,139. The number of bodies recovered from under the rubble since then has reached 807.

items.title: National unity minister says Orang Asal heritage part of Malaysia’s national identity, not separate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The heritage of Malaysia’s indigenous peoples (Orang Asal) is part of the country’s national legacy and identity, rather than belonging solely to the communities themselves, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said. In a Facebook post marking the 2026 International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples today, he said efforts to empower indigenous communities should move in tandem with national development without allowing their languages, customs and traditional knowledge to become marginalised. “Malaysia is fortunate to have indigenous communities that are an important part of the country’s history and identity.

items.title: MBPP blames root rot and trunk cavity for Angsana collapse in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Root rot and a cavity in the base of a 90-year-old Angsana tree, compounded by chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space, contributed to its collapse along Jalan Macalister here today. MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall tree, Pterocarpus indicus, had an estimated 30 per cent root rot, while cavity decay accounted for about 40 per cent of its base trunk. He said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being identified for felling, all of which had since been removed.

items.title: Sarawak chokes under haze blanket as hot weather grips state until Aug 14
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Most parts of Sarawak will be experiencing hot weather and reduced rainfall until August 14, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. In addition, southern Sarawak is set to experience transboundary haze due to increased hotspots in the neighbouring country, he said. “Analysis of the latest weather forecast models indicate that hot weather and below-average rainfall are expected in most parts of Borneo, including Sarawak, until August 14.

items.title: Malaysian tahfiz student killed, friend injured after motorcycle crashes into pole in Yala
items.summary: YALA, Aug 9 — A Malaysian man was killed while his friend was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding was involved in an accident in the Bannang Sareng area, Mueang Yala district, on Saturday afternoon. Mueang Yala Police Chief Col Chatchai Sakdee said preliminary investigations found that the victim lost control of the motorcycle before crashing into an electricity pole. Chatchai said the injured victim is currently receiving treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) at Yala Central Hospital and remains unconscious.

items.title: Terengganu police arrest three Myanmar men over sexual offence against disabled woman
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 9 — Three Myanmar male refugees working as construction and cleaning workers were detained in connection with a sexual case involving an intellectually disabled woman in this district yesterday. Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the three men, aged between 19 and 28, were arrested after receiving a report regarding the alleged sexual case from a 20-year-old woman on Friday. He said that the public is advised not to make any baseless speculation as the case is still under police investigation.

items.title: Police lodge report after fake statement linked to deputy IGP spreads on Facebook
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has denied a viral social media post falsely linked to the deputy Inspector-General of Police (IGP), stressing that the content was fabricated and misleading. “PDRM stresses that the post is fake. The deputy IGP has never held such a press conference or issued any statement as claimed,” the force said in a statement issued by DCP Datuk Mohamad Noor Yusof Ali, secretary of the Royal Malaysia Police.

items.title: Military veterans need more second-career opportunities, says Dr Wan Azizah
items.summary: SERI KEMBANGAN, Aug 9 — The private sector needs to expand second-career opportunities for military veterans as part of efforts to strengthen their welfare and empowerment, says ‘Kempen Tabung Pahlawan’ (Warriors Fund Campaign) patron Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. She said the private sector also played an important role in ensuring military veterans got the opportunity to continue contributing to society and the nation after ending their service with the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF). A total of RM220,000 was raised from eight private companies through MYGCC 2026, in conjunction with Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, reinforcing the programme’s role as a fundraising platform for military veterans’ welfare.

items.title: Melaka seat swaps on the table for Perikatan, Samsuri tells BN
items.summary: TAIPING, Aug 9 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is open to talks with Barisan Nasional (BN), including possible seat swaps, ahead of the Melaka state election, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today. Utusan Malaysia reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying no formal discussions had taken place, but there was still sufficient time for the parties to consider electoral cooperation before the Melaka state assembly is dissolved. Ahmad Samsuri said any discussions would ideally take place before the state assembly is dissolved to give the parties sufficient time to prepare for the election.

items.title: Melaka Pakatan open to talks, coalition welcomes negotiations ahead state election
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 9 — Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to negotiations with any party for the upcoming Melaka State Election, said its chairman Adly Zahari. He said the form of cooperation and number of seats to be contested have yet to be finalised, with two series of meetings held so far to assess the coalition’s prospects, while preparations for the state election remain focused internally within PH. Commenting on seat targets, Adly said Melaka PH is optimistic about increasing its number of State Legislative Assembly seats from the five seats it previously won out of a total of 28.

items.title: Driver forgot to put SUV in park before crashing into KKIA departure hall, police say
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Police said preliminary investigations indicate that a 66-year-old woman forgot to put her SUV in parking gear before it rolled forward and crashed into the glass doors of Kota Kinabalu International Airport’s (KKIA) departure hall on Friday. Berita Harian reported Kota Kinabalu police chief ACP Shahrudin Mat Husain as saying the woman had stopped in the airport’s second lane to pick up her child and was preparing to switch drivers when the incident occurred. Shahrudin said the SUV then surged forward, struck another vehicle and crashed through the departure hall’s glass doors before hitting a building pillar.

items.title: Samsuri says Bersatu remains in Perikatan despite Hadi’s claim
items.summary: TAIPING, Aug 9 — Bersatu remains a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) despite claims that its membership had automatically lapsed over plans for a new political coalition, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today. Utusan Malaysia reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying Bersatu’s status in PN had not changed as of today. PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang had on Friday claimed that Bersatu was no longer part of PN after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition.

items.title: Umno‑PAS pact not for Sabah, Salleh Keruak says politics driven by autonomy rights
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Any political understanding between Umno and PAS that may work in Peninsular Malaysia may not necessarily be suitable for Sabah, where political realities are markedly different, said Umno Sabah treasurer Datuk Seri Salleh Said Keruak. He said the 2025 Sabah State Election had clearly demonstrated the strength of Sabah-based political sentiment, with local interests, autonomy, development and Sabah’s rights increasingly influencing voters’ choices. Salleh said Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) won 29 of the 55 seats it contested in the state election, while Parti Warisan (Warisan) secured 25 of the 73 seats it contested.

items.title: Prasarana to run 24-hour public transport services for National Day, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad will operate public transport services around the clock from the night of August 30 into August 31 for this year’s National Day celebrations, Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil reportedly said today. “Prasarana has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with National Day 2026,” he was quoted as saying. Fahmi also said that this year’s Malaysia Day celebration on September 16 would be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Kuching, Sarawak.

items.title: DAP congress set for Aug 16 showdown, stalled reforms and grassroots frustration to dominate agenda
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — National DAP organising secretary Datuk Chan Foong Hin said concerns over the lack of progress on institutional reforms, partly due to insufficient parliamentary support, will be addressed at the party’s national congress on August 16. “Without adequate support, it is difficult to carry out major reforms,” he said, questioning the absence of BN backbenchers. Chan also described Malaysia’s current political landscape as “blurred”, citing recent political developments in Peninsular Malaysia following state election results, including the appearance of opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin alongside figures aligned with the ruling bloc.

items.title: Sarawak haze thickens, Serian tops API at 170 as Kuching, Bintulu readings hit 155
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Miri and Sarikei recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 1pm today. According to the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight districts are now recording unhealthy API levels, including Miri (118) and Sarikei (147). Other monitoring stations across the state recorded moderate API readings, ranging from 74 to 92.

items.title: Malaysia Day 2026 celebration set for Kuching’s Borneo Convention Centre, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The 2026 Malaysia Day celebration will be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. Fahmi said preparations for the Malaysia Day celebration were progressing smoothly, with the next meeting scheduled for August 24 to further discuss arrangements for the event. Meanwhile, he said Prasarana Malaysia Bhd has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with the National Day celebration in Putrajaya on August 31.

items.title: Minister warns unregistered marriages risk children’s rights, complicate birth certificates, education
items.summary: LABUAN, Aug 9 — Unregistered marriages can have serious implications on children’s rights and family welfare, including difficulties in obtaining birth certificates, accessing education and healthcare, as well as inheritance matters, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. The effects are significant and far-reaching,” he said when launching the 2026 Federal Territories Syariah Law Literacy Programme at Kompleks Darul Kifayah here today. Zulkifli said the department, together with religious agencies and strategic partners, was taking a proactive approach to addressing outstanding marriage registration and marriage verification issues among residents.

items.title: Three freed after fallen tree traps them inside car in George Town
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Three people were rescued after a tree fell on the Perodua Ativa they were travelling in along Jalan Macalister this morning. The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 9.12am and dispatched eight firefighters from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene. “All three victims who were trapped inside the vehicle were successfully freed by members of the public before the rescue team arrived,” the department said.

items.title: Malaysia awaits US response on excess capacity after concluding forced-labour tariff talks, says Johari Ghani
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 9 — Malaysia is awaiting Washington’s response on concerns over industrial excess capacity after completing the forced-labour component of its discussions with the US, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today. The Star reported that Johari, speaking at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia’s (ACCCIM) 80th annual general meeting here, said the government would continue engaging the US on the outstanding issue. Under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, Malaysia has committed to prohibit imports made using forced labour as well as take steps to address global excess capacity in the steel sector.

items.title: Myanmar refugee figures soon, Saifuddin Nasution vows biometric drive for repatriation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — Preliminary data on Myanmar refugees who are currently identified through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme is expected to be obtained in the fourth quarter of this year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Home Ministry (KDN) through the Immigration Department (JIM) is implementing the data collection process with relevant parties. “We are conducting a data collection.

items.title: 'Wishing them a speedy recovery': Anwar visits Ismail Sabri and Fadillah at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof and former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who are both receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN), yesterday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he made the visits with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, was admitted to IJN on August 6 after experiencing health issues while having his statement recorded at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission headquarters.

items.title: Pakatan hails BN openness, Fahmi says Melaka seat talks offer chance for stability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) welcomes the openness of Barisan Nasional (BN) regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and describes it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined. “The chairman of Keadilan Melaka, Yang Berhormat Adam Adli, also informed that he had been in direct contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof (regarding the distribution of Melaka State Legislative Assembly seats). Fahmi, who is also the Communications Minister, said in this regard several matters could be managed at the state and federal levels regarding the distribution of state seats in Melaka.

items.title: Bersatu turns to RoS after Hadi says party automatically out of Perikatan
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) reportedly plans to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over claims that its Perikatan Nasional (PN) membership had automatically lapsed after the party expressed its intention to form a new political coalition. “PN is not PAS. PN must be managed in accordance with the PN constitution, fairly, transparently and with integrity, without denying the rights of its members.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution vows scanner upgrade, promises smarter baggage checks after pilot drug scandal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — The government will look into upgrading scanning machines at airports nationwide as part of efforts to strengthen security and improve the effectiveness of baggage screening, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the government was always open to exploring the use of the latest screening equipment in line with technological advancements, particularly at the country’s main entry points. Saifuddin Nasution said baggage screening at airports was the responsibility of the Aviation Security (AVSEC) team and was in line with international airport screening standards under the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).

items.title: Govt ends 40-year settlement issue with land grants for 120 Perak families, says housing minister
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 9 — A total of 120 squatter families around Sungkai and Kuala Bikam have been given land grants, resolving a settlement issue they had faced for more than 40 years, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. In a statement last night, Nga said the resolution of the issue was proof that the Madani Government always prioritised the wellbeing of the people regardless of racial background and social status, in line with its commitment to ensuring no Malaysian was left behind or marginalised in development. Last night, 120 families are receiving land grants that symbolise a more secure future for them and future generations,” he said.

items.title: Immigration investigates video of vehicle reportedly misusing department logo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The Immigration Department is investigating the use of its logo on a vehicle seen in a viral social media post and reportedly driven by a foreign national. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle did not belong to the department and was not one of its official assets. The department said investigations were under way to identify the individual involved and determine the purpose behind the use of its logo on the vehicle.

items.title: Perlis Umno gears up to contest all seats solo at next election
items.summary: ARAU, Aug 9 — Perlis Umno is preparing its machinery to contest all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies on its own at the next election, state liaison chairman Datuk Rozabil Abd Rahman reprotedly said. Berita Harian reported that Rozabil said there had so far been no official talks with any political party, including Perikatan Nasional (PN), on electoral cooperation in Perlis. He said the state chapter, which failed to win any seat in Perlis at the last election, would leave any eventual decision on electoral cooperation to the party’s national leadership.

items.title: Five Sarawak areas record unhealthy API levels amid transboundary haze
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 9 — Five areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am today, compared with six areas yesterday afternoon. Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings were Kuching (153), Samarahan (156), Serian (170), Bintulu (156) and Samalaju (151). Uggah, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the areas identified were Betong, Bintulu, Daro, Julau, Kanowit, Kuching, Lundu, Marudi, Miri, Mukah, Pakan, Samarahan, Saratok, Serian, Sibu, Simunjan, Song, Sri Aman and Tatau.
